raw_response:
I’m 58, been on this land 40 years. Only primary school, but I know these 10 mu better than any textbook. My wife and me, just the two of us now — the kids are in Shijiazhuang working factory jobs. We grow cotton, always have.

I’m putting all 10 mu in cotton again. I thought about that wheat-maize double crop like Lao Zhang down the road, but I don’t have the machinery for that rush between harvest and planting, and honestly I don’t trust it. Cotton is what I know. I’ll plant around April 20th when the dirt warms up. I buy hybrid seed from the ag shop — about one and a half jin per mu, costs around 60 yuan. My own saved seed never grows as strong.

For fertilizer, I put down about 30 jin of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant — that’s my base, same as always. Then when the plants flower in July, I topdress with about 30 jin of urea. Last year the extension fellow told me to use less, so I cut back on my south plot and the yield dropped bad. Never again. I’d rather spend the extra money than lose half a crop. A bad year hurts worse than a good year helps — that’s what my father taught me.

I’ll water twice from the well. First time when they flower in July, second time in August when the bolls are filling. Pumping costs me about 40 yuan per mu each time, plus the electricity. It’s not cheap, but without water in July the cotton just sits there and wilts.

Bollworm is the devil. I spray four times — herbicide before planting, then insecticide when seedlings are up, at squaring, at flowering, and once more in August if I see damage. The chemical runs about 25 yuan per mu per spray. Some years I can skip the last one, but last August the worms came bad so I’m budgeting for all four.

My wife and I do all the field work — I plow with the small tractor in early April, then we plant, weed, fertilize, spray, and irrigate together. But picking in September and October? No way two of us can pick 10 mu. We’ll hire local women, probably 20 days total. I pay them 120 to 150 yuan a day depending on how much they pick. That’s my biggest cash outlay, but cotton doesn’t pick itself.

I’m figuring on about 260 kg of lint per mu if the weather treats us right. Last year I got about that. The soil is decent, I know the timing, and I’m not trying anything new this year. New things are risky when you’re small like me.
